blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Query-based camera-radar detectors choose where and over which frames each object query samples from the query's position or feature. We test whether radar evidence around the query should also set these choices at the 150 m range of MAN TruckScenes, where recall differs across object-level radar-return counts within every range band. EviScope is a minimal test: the current frame's returns form a non-learned bird's-eye evidence field, which each query reads at its decoded centre to scale its radial sampling extent and to weight eight frames. It adds 5,450 parameters (0.009%) to RaCFormer, with no latency increase in our timing. Our module-free recipe exceeds the published TruckScenes mAP (25.9 over seven runs against 24.1), so we measure the module only against its own baseline at matched seeds. The evidence a query reads rises with its object's return count (Spearman 0.51) but captures zero-return objects only in part, and the learned radius tracks it ($ρ\approx-0.91$ in four runs). Over seven four-epoch pairs the module changes NDS by $+0.31\pm0.36$ and mAP by $-0.27\pm0.22$ (mean $\pm$ SE). Against a geometry-only conditioner with the same parameter count, trained at three matched seeds, it is higher by $+1.25\pm0.72$ NDS and $+0.87\pm0.21$ mAP, on mAP in every pair, and the control's mean NDS is near the baseline's. An exploratory far-range gain failed an internally pre-specified held-out test, and large inference-time substitution penalties also occur without query-local evidence: neither learned allocation nor inference-time dependence substitutes for matched end-to-end comparisons.

blocks.en:
Camera–radar fusion combines the semantic detail of vision with radar’s range
and velocity measurements for long-range 3D object detection ( Fent et al., 2024 ; Nabati & Qi, 2021 ; Kim et al., 2023b ; Lin et al., 2024b ) . Detectors of this kind are
query-based: they refine a fixed set of object queries over successive decoder
layers and sample image and bird’s-eye-view (BEV) features from each query’s
position ( Carion et al., 2020 ; Wang et al., 2021b ; Liu et al., 2022 ; Liu et al., 2023a ) . Recent work exploits
geometric structure through concentric query initialisation with adaptive
sampling ( Chu et al., 2025 ) , distance-modulated radar aggregation ( Wolters et al., 2024 ) ,
or object-centred Gaussian representations ( Bang et al., 2026 ) . We investigate
whether explicit local radar evidence provides conditioning information for
query sampling beyond query geometry.

blocks.en:
We propose EviScope , an evidence-conditioned query sampling framework that
adapts the spatial sampling extent and the temporal aggregation weights while
keeping the query position as the geometric reference. Current-frame radar
returns form a parameter-free BEV evidence field of multiscale return counts and
radar measurement statistics. Each query reads this field at its decoded centre
and combines the descriptor with its own geometry through a lightweight shared
network. A spatial branch and a temporal branch then predict a radial sampling
scale and a weighting over the eight fused frames, so queries at similar
positions but with different evidence sample differently; a training-only
density branch supervises the shared representation. The change is
small: one non-learned input conditions two sampling controls that RaCFormer
already has. Matched-capacity controls test its contribution;
Table 15 separates inherited and added components. It
adds 5,450 5{,}450 parameters, 0.009 % 0.009\% of the detector, with no latency increase
in our timing protocol.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Long-range camera–radar 3D detection. Camera–radar fusion builds on
the camera-only BEV lineage ( Philion & Fidler, 2020 ; Huang et al., 2021 ; Li et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2022 ) and is organised around object-level association, BEV fusion, and sparse
cross-modal interaction. At the object level, Nabati & Qi (2021) associate
radar detections with image objects through a frustum and Kim et al. (2023a) exchange spatial and contextual cues between proposals with cross-attention. In
BEV, Kim et al. (2023b) use radar to assist the view transform and absorb the residual
misalignment with multi-modal deformable attention, while Lin et al. (2024b) align the branches with a radar-specific encoder and cross-modal attention,
a design Lin et al. (2024a) extend to query-based detectors ( Wolters et al., 2025 , see also) . At truck range the cost of dense interaction binds:
4D-radar benchmarks ( Palffy et al., 2022 ; Paek et al., 2022 ) annotate shorter ranges, and the
entries that reach 150 150 m on TruckScenes ( Fent et al., 2024 ) turn sparse: Wolters et al. (2024) fuse inside sparse
frusta with range-adaptive radar aggregation, and Bang et al. (2026) build a
sparse representation from primitives at estimated keypoints ( Li et al., 2025 , see also) . All of them allocate sampling by position
(Section 1 ).

returns are uncertain and the two modalities differ in observation quality ( Huang et al., 2025 ) . Long et al. (2025) predict the distribution of returns an object

blocks.en:
Query-driven adaptive spatio-temporal sampling. Query-based detectors
use their observations through spatial sampling and aggregation across frames. Wang et al. (2021b) project a 3D reference into the multi-view images; Li et al. (2022) fuse past BEV features with temporal self-attention; Lin et al. (2023) propagate sparse instance features recurrently instead of
re-sampling every past image. Liu et al. (2023a) generate sampling offsets in
space and time from the query feature and mix the sampled features with
predicted weights, and Chu et al. (2025) combine polar initialisation with
cross-view and cross-modal ray sampling. These policies condition on position
or the query feature; we supply local radar statistics as an explicit,
non-learned input to the spatial scale and the temporal weights, and test what
that input adds beyond geometry (Appendix T ).

We test whether current-frame local radar evidence can guide a query’s
sampling extent and temporal aggregation. Sparse evidence motivates a wider
search and a different weighting of past frames, but does not identify which
past frames contain useful returns. We implemented this as a small addition to RaCFormer ( Chu et al., 2025 ) , shown in Figure 2 . We use MAN TruckScenes ( Fent et al., 2024 ) under the official detection_cvpr_2024 protocol: 12 classes, centre-distance matching at { 0.5 , 1 , 2 , 4 } \{0.5,1,2,4\} m, cars scored to 150 150 m, following the protocol inherited

camera and radar only, with no LiDAR at inference or as depth supervision. The
detector is RaCFormer ( Chu et al., 2025 ) with a ResNet-50 backbone ( He et al., 2016 ) at 256 × 704 256\times 704 input; every row we train uses class-balanced
resampling ( Zhu et al., 2019 ) , eight temporal frames and four epochs on one node of
eight A100 GPUs at an effective batch of eight. We call this configuration
without the module the baseline , and the same configuration with the
module EviScope . Where we report several runs, the runs differ only in the
random seed, which sets the initialisation and the data order; the samplers are
not deterministic, so two runs at the same seed would also differ.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced EviScope to test radar evidence as an additional signal for
query sampling in camera–radar detection. On TruckScenes, the module-free
recipe exceeds the published mAP values in our comparison, while seven
matched pairs leave the module’s incremental benefit unresolved: + 0.31 ± 0.36 +0.31\pm 0.36 NDS and − 0.27 ± 0.22 -0.27\pm 0.22 mAP (mean ± \pm SE).
Against a geometry-only conditioner of the same size, EviScope is
higher by + 0.87 ± 0.21 +0.87\pm 0.21 mAP and + 1.25 ± 0.72 +1.25\pm 0.72 NDS over three matched seeds. An exploratory subset gain fails an
internally pre-specified test on two further seeds, and large temporal
substitution penalties also occur without correctly aligned query-local
evidence. These findings support evaluating learned allocation,
inference-time dependence and paired detection gains separately. Evaluation
beyond this benchmark remains necessary to assess the broader hypothesis.
